cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: Ancient philosophy is not just about talking or lecturing, or even reading long, dense

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: books.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: In fact, it is something people have used throughout history – to solve their problems

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: and to achieve their greatest triumphs.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: Specifically, I am referring to Stoicism, which, in my opinion, is the most practical of

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: all philosophies and therefore the most appealing.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: Stoicism was founded in Ancient Greece by Zeno of Citium in the early 3rd century BC, but

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: was practised by the likes of Epictetus, Cato.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: Seneca and Marcus Aurelius.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: Amazingly, we still have access to these ideas, despite the fact that the most famous

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: Stoics never wrote anything down for publication. Cato definitely didn't.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: Marcus Aurelius never intended his Meditations to be anything but personal.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: Seneca's letters were, well, letters and Epictetus' thoughts come to us by way of a

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: note-taking student.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: Stoic principles were based on the idea that its followers could have an unshakable

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: happiness in this life and the key to achieving this was virtue.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: The road to virtue, in turn, lay in understanding that destructive emotions, like anger

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: and jealousy, are under our conscious control – they don't have to control us, because we

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: can learn to control them.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: In the words of Epictetus: “external events I cannot control, but the choices I

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: make with regard to them, I do control”.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: The modern day philosopher and writer Nassim Nicholas Taleb defines a Stoic as someone

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: who has a different perspective on experience which most of us would see as wholly

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: negative; a Stoic “transforms fear into caution, pain into transformation, mistakes

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: into initiation and desire into undertaking”.

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: Using this definition as a model, we can see that throughout the centuries Stoicism has

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: been practised in more recent history by kings, presidents, artists, writers and

cues.speaker: OM
cues.text: entrepreneurs.
